claims.text: Applying a nanocrystalline HEA interlayer at W–Cu interfaces will increase the composite's thermal conductivity.
A W–Cu composite containing the HEA interlayer will retain mechanical durability.
A W–Cu composite containing the HEA interlayer will retain irradiation resistance.
Conventional W–Cu composites contain distinct tungsten and copper phases.
Conventional W–Cu composites have relatively high W–Cu interfacial thermal resistance.
The proposed intervention is to introduce a thin nanocrystalline HEA coating at W–Cu interfaces during fabrication.
The predicted benefits are intended to hold under fusion-reactor joint conditions involving high thermal loads, temperature cycling, and irradiation.
The intervention will produce a continuous, nanocrystalline HEA layer at the W–Cu boundaries.
The HEA interlayer will enhance bonding between tungsten and copper.
The nanocrystalline HEA interlayer will minimize interfacial thermal-phonon scattering.
The HEA interlayer provides a graded transition between tungsten and copper.
The graded transition reduces interfacial mismatch between tungsten and copper.
Reducing W–Cu interfacial mismatch lowers interfacial thermal resistance.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys have demonstrated high thermal stability.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys have demonstrated resistance to heavy-ion, dual-beam, and helium irradiation, including low defect evolution and no detectable grain growth.
The irradiation and thermal stability of the HEA interlayer will preserve the mechanical integrity of the W–Cu composite under extreme conditions.
The HEA-interlayer composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable W–Cu composite without the interlayer.
The HEA-interlayer composite will have mechanical durability comparable to the control W–Cu composite.
The HEA-interlayer composite will have irradiation resistance comparable to the control W–Cu composite.
Nonuniformity or deviations in interlayer thickness, continuity, or composition may eliminate the improvement or degrade composite performance.
